answer: Unique-action certificate auction: each agent buys a certificate binding one key to one measured resource unit, priced higher when requests share a source fingerprint, a terrace of linked submissions. A duplicate identity must pay the full cluster marginal price plus an ivory audit fee, so an N-key syndicate pays N times the marginal certificate. Each certificate writes a signed crystal log entry, making key reuse auditable and forcing attackers to absorb that per-key price.
